build.summary:
Built the procedural audio engine in src/game/audio (no audio files, no dependencies, no three.js; 15.2 KB minified / 5.8 KB gzip for the four runtime files). `createAudio: CreateAudio` is exported from src/game/audio/index.ts.

What it contains: (1) synth.ts - one `voice()` primitive (sine/triangle/square/saw/25% pulse/noise, envelope, glide, vibrato, filter sweep, tremolo) that takes a BaseAudioContext, so the same code runs live and in an OfflineAudioContext; plus the mixer: sfx bus + music bus -> stateless soft-knee limiter -> master gain 0.5 (mute ramps here), with a shared echo send. (2) sfx.ts - all 17 SfxName effects as original recipes. (3) music.ts - three original tunes in a compact note notation and a step sequencer: title (G major, 4/4, 132 bpm, 8 bars, 14.545 s), lobby (F major, 3/4, 104 bpm, 16 bars, 27.692 s, percussion enters in the second half), course (the lobby harmony as a slow music-box arpeggio, 84 bpm, 16 bars, 34.286 s, no percussion). Lead + bass + light percussion at most. (4) index.ts - lifecycle, look-ahead scheduler on the AudioContext clock (250 ms window, 40 ms wake-up), cross-fade, mute, suspend/resume, dispose, per-effect rate limiting, all public methods wrapped so nothing throws. (5) offline.ts - offline rendering helpers (dev only, not in the game bundle).

Harness: /dev/audio with buttons for unlock, every effect (with volume and rate sliders), each track, silence, mute, suspend, resume, dispose, a live status line, and four scripted checks: window.__audioTest(), __audioMixTest(), __audioLifecycleTest(), __audioLiveTest(track). The page also draws a waveform and spectrogram per item so the sounds can be judged by eye.

Two real defects were found and fixed through the tests: a DynamicsCompressorNode on the master swallowed about 8 dB of the first ~100 ms after unlock (it would have dulled the PRESS START chime), so the limiter is now a wave-shaper; and Chrome plays the first few ms of an oscillator at the default 440 Hz when its pitch is only set by setValueAtTime at the start time, so start values are now written to param.value.

Important caveat: the shared dev server on localhost:3000 stopped responding part-way through (connection refused, nothing listening). I did not restart it. Everything after that was verified by transpiling the same source files into a file:// page driven by the same headless Chrome driver. Nobody has listened to these sounds; all evidence is numeric or visual. The request to "also use multi agents" could not be acted on here: this session has no tool for spawning agents.
verification: Type-check: `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` exits 0 with no errors at the end of the task (mid-task it briefly reported two errors in src/game/engine/game.ts, another engineer's file, which cleared on their side).

Dev server runs (before it went down): `node tools/shot.mjs http://localhost:3000/dev/audio --steps '[{"eval":"window.__audioTest()"}]'` returned 20 rows, none silent, none clipping, and the Next-rendered harness page was screenshotted and inspected: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-faviojasso-Library-Application-Support-Claude-scratch-workspaces-2e78f3bf-6b09-4892-8e37-05d4f25b71e0-0f59886b-c83f-4098-9822-b751fbbcfb93-scratch-2026-11-10-cf9e80/381bbed9-222e-45b2-b07f-9df9e8e2450e/scratchpad/shots/audio/offline-1.png, offline-2.png, big-a.png, big-b.png, big-c.png, big2-a.png, big2-b.png (same folder). Those runs predate the final level tuning.

Final-state runs used a static fallback because localhost:3000 refused connections: scratchpad/scripts/audio-bundle.cjs transpiles the unmodified source files into scratchpad/audio-static/index.html, driven with the same shot.mjs and the same evals.

window.__audioTest() final table (output peak / RMS / pre-limiter peak / scheduled length s; all silent=false, clipping=false): start 0.260/0.051/0.520/1.03; uiMove 0.195/0.037/0.390/0.06; uiSelect 0.191/0.034/0.381/0.24; uiBack 0.188/0.034/0.376/0.24; pause 0.140/0.024/0.280/0.39; unpause 0.141/0.025/0.282/0.39; doorOpen 0.287/0.056/0.574/0.79; doorClose 0.307/0.051/0.615/0.19; step 0.132/0.028/0.263/0.045; jump 0.247/0.042/0.493/0.17; land 0.276/0.053/0.551/0.11; dive 0.228/0.034/0.456/0.44; warpIn 0.290/0.100/0.580/0.95; warpOut 0.290/0.102/0.582/0.95; starGet 0.230/0.052/0.460/1.02; starPose 0.334/0.085/0.674/1.57; snore 0.213/0.033/0.426/1.58; title (8 s) 0.133/0.026/0.266; lobby (8 s) 0.117/0.033/0.234; course (8 s) 0.086/0.027/0.172. Highest output peak anywhere is 0.334 against the 0.98 clipping line; every pre-limiter peak is under 0.7, so nothing would clip even without the limiter.

Pitch direction measured from the renders (dominant Hz at 20% -> 80%): start 1109->1317 (rising), uiSelect 881->1317 (up a fifth), uiBack 783->522 (down a fifth), jump 346->551, warpIn 279->843, warpOut 828->274 (mirror), starGet 1317->1977, doorClose 100->57, land 146->80.

Loop length and seamlessness (window.__audioMixTest, three passes of each loop rendered at a sample rate where a step is a whole number of samples): title 14.545 s, lobby 27.692 s, course 34.286 s; every voice written to exactly the loop's step count (128/128/128, 96/96/96, 96/96/-); third pass minus second pass = -146.7 / -145.6 / -146.1 dB (effectively identical); the same comparison one bar short = +2.4 / +2.6 / +2.5 dB (so the period really is the full loop); level in the half second around the seam within 1.1 dB of the loop average; largest sample-to-sample jump at the seam is smaller than elsewhere in the loop (no click).

Live scheduler vs offline render (runLiveTest: real AudioContext output captured through a ScriptProcessor across the loop seam, then subtracted from the offline render): title 17.05 s, error -69.7 dB, worst 0.25 s window -47.6 dB; lobby 30.19 s, -132.7 dB; course 36.79 s, -128.0 dB. No dropped, late or doubled notes.

play() options: volume 0.5 gives exactly x0.5 pre-limiter peak; rate 2 gives x0.5 length and x2.001 pitch; step pitch variation spans x1.174 between the extremes of the pseudo-random input (no Math.random anywhere in the module).

Cross-fade envelope measured against an unfaded render: outgoing track gain 0.487 / 0.227 / 0.056 / 0.002 and incoming 0.534 / 0.779 / 0.944 / 0.998 at 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.4 / 0.8 s; output peak during a lobby->title cross-fade 0.111 vs 0.110 around it (no bump).

Mix: music mean RMS -30.9 dBFS vs effects -25.7 dBFS (effects 5.2 dB louder; music output peaks 0.086-0.133 vs effects 0.13-0.33). Worst-case pile-up (lobby music + doorOpen, jump, step, dive, warpIn, starGet, starPose inside 0.7 s): pre-limiter peak 1.20, output peak 0.471, not clipping.

Awkward call orders (window.__audioLifecycleTest, live AudioContext in headless Chrome): 30 of 30 checks pass - play/setMusic/setMuted/suspend/resume before unlock create nothing; unlock starts the remembered track and honours a mute set earlier (analyser reads silence); play() immediately after unlock() is accepted; unlock is idempotent (one context); setMusic with the current track twice does not restart it; four stacked cross-fades with mute toggled mid-fade end on the right track and the faded players are released; 60 rapid step calls schedule exactly one; all 17 effects play with volume and rate options; NaN/Infinity/negative/zero options and unknown names do not throw; suspend freezes the context clock and drops effects; resume continues the same loop position; unlock resumes a suspended context; setMusic(null) fades to silence and releases the track; dispose closes the context; every call after dispose is safe; unlock after dispose starts fresh with the mute preference kept; with AudioContext removed, and with a constructor that throws, every call is a silent no-op.

Harness page behaviour: the real page component was mounted with React (StrictMode) from a file:// bundle (scratchpad/scripts/audio-bundle-page.cjs) and driven by clicking its buttons; the status line tracked each action correctly (lobby playing -> effects counted -> MUTED -> cross-fade showing 2 players then 1 -> suspended with a frozen step -> resumed -> silence -> locked after Dispose -> re-unlocks on the next effect), and ?run=all rendered all three result sections with every badge OK. Screenshot: scratchpad/shots/audio/static-page-all.png. Spectrogram gallery of the final sounds: scratchpad/shots/audio/gallery-0.png, gallery-1.png, gallery-2.png.

Harmony check (scratchpad/scripts/audio-theory.py): every bar of all three tunes sums to the right length, and the only lead/bass intervals flagged are intended ones (a passing major seventh, two dominant-seventh tritones, one 9-8 suspension).

Size and imports (scratchpad/scripts/audio-size.cjs, using Next's bundled terser): synth 3.1 KB, sfx 4.0 KB, music 4.8 KB, index 3.2 KB minified; 5.8 KB gzip total. Runtime imports are only ./synth, ./sfx, ./music and type-only imports from ../contract.
knownIssues: The dev server on http://localhost:3000 became unreachable during the task (connection refused, no process listening on the port) and was still down when I finished. I did not start or restart anything. The final code was therefore not re-run through the Next-served /dev/audio page; it was verified through a file:// harness built from the same source files. The Next-rendered page was last seen working before the final tuning (limiter swap, level changes, live test hook), and its results sections were only seen rendered in the static React mount, which has globals.css but no Tailwind utility classes.

Nobody has listened to any of this. Levels, pitch contours, envelopes, loop timing and harmony are measured; whether each sound is actually pleasant, and whether the tunes are enjoyable on repeat, is unverified by ear and should be checked by a person on the harness page.
Only headless Chrome on macOS was exercised. Safari, iOS (including the silent-buffer unlock path and the hardware mute switch) and Firefox are untested.
Originality rests on the fact that I composed the melodies and designed the effects from scratch; there is no automated way to prove a melody resembles nothing that exists.

doorClose, land and the percussion thump carry most of their energy below 150 Hz and will be faint on phone and laptop speakers; each has a mid-range knock or noise layer so it does not vanish, but they will sound much fuller on headphones.
The limiter is a wave-shaper, so an extreme pile-up (pre-limiter level above about 1) is softly saturated rather than ducked. In the measured worst case this stayed well below clipping.

The scheduler is woken by setInterval. If the tab is hidden and the engine does not call suspend(), browser timer throttling will make the music drop notes (late notes are skipped, never fired in a burst).

In headless Chrome the audio device took 0.4-2 s to start its clock after unlock; sounds requested in that window are held and play when it starts (at most four are allowed to queue). Real browsers are normally much faster, but the first chime can never start before the device opens.
No sub-agents were used despite the request to use multiple agents: this session has no agent-spawning tool.
contractGaps: None blocking. The AudioEngine interface was sufficient as written.

The contract does not say what `unlocked` means when Web Audio is unavailable. I return false in that case (no context exists); the stub returned true after any unlock() call. UI that shows a 'sound unavailable' state can rely on this, UI that waits for `unlocked` before enabling something should not.

The contract does not say whether dispose() is terminal. Because services.ts hands out one shared engine for the whole page, I made dispose() return the engine to its locked state (mute preference kept, requested track cleared) so a remount, including React StrictMode's double mount, can unlock it again.

For tests I added a non-contract `createAudioEngine()` export whose result also has `inspect()` (context state, clock, playing track, loop position, counters, master node). `createAudio` returns the same object typed as plain AudioEngine.
integrationNotes: Flip src/game/services.ts to `import { createAudio } from "./audio"` in place of the stub. Nothing else needs to change; the module never touches window until unlock().

Call unlock() inside the PRESS START (or any first) user gesture. play("start") straight after unlock() in the same handler works and is covered by a test. Calling unlock() on later gestures is harmless and also revives a context the browser suspended.
setMusic() before unlock is remembered and starts on unlock; setMuted() before unlock is honoured. dispose() clears the remembered track, so call setMusic() again after re-creating the game.

The audio module does not listen for visibilitychange itself: the engine must call suspend() when the tab is hidden and resume() when it is shown, as the contract describes. Effects requested while suspended are dropped, not queued.

Rate limits are built in, so calling per frame is safe: step at most every 0.12 s, snore every 2.8 s (longer than the 1.6 s sound, so a sleeping avatar breathes at a natural pace), doorOpen every 0.2 s, everything else every 40 ms per effect name.

play() options: volume is clamped to 0-2 (0 skips the sound), rate to 0.25-4 and it scales pitch and speed together; NaN or Infinity fall back to 1. step already varies its own pitch by about 8% either way.

Levels live in src/game/audio/synth.ts: MASTER_GAIN 0.5, SFX_GAIN 1.2, MUSIC_GAIN 0.26. Music is deliberately about 5 dB under the effects; raise MUSIC_GAIN if it feels too quiet once someone has listened.

Harness: /dev/audio; add ?run=1 to run the offline test on load, ?run=all for offline + mix + lifecycle, ?big=1 for tall waveforms and spectrograms. The headless driver reports one failed request for va.vercel-scripts.com (the analytics script in the root layout), which is unrelated to audio.

If the dev server is still down when integrating, the two fallback scripts in the scratchpad (scripts/audio-bundle.cjs and scripts/audio-bundle-page.cjs) rebuild the file:// harness from the current sources.
blueprintDeviations: The blueprint's 'classic' start chime, door creak, warp sound and pause chime are replaced by original synthesized sounds, as the build guide's substitution table requires. No melody, rhythm signature or timbre was taken from an existing game.

Master limiter: a stateless soft-knee wave-shaper instead of a DynamicsCompressorNode. The brief allowed either; the compressor measurably attenuated the first ~100 ms after the context starts by about 8 dB (output peak 0.094 instead of 0.236 for the same sound), which would have dulled the PRESS START chime, and it adds 6 ms of latency.

The lobby tune is in 3/4 rather than the more usual 4/4, a deliberate choice to make it stately and clearly its own piece. The course track is written as a variation on the lobby's harmony rather than an unrelated tune.
Lobby percussion plays only in the second eight bars, to give the 28-second loop some shape on repeat.

review.summary: I reviewed the Audio module (src/game/audio/**, src/app/dev/audio/**) and tested it against the live dev server at http://localhost:3000/dev/audio, which was up for this review. The builder's report holds up. All 17 SfxName effects render as non-silent and below the clipping line. The three loops repeat with a pass-to-pass difference of about -145 dB, and the live scheduler matches the offline render. The engine is silent and creates nothing before unlock(), and the mute, suspend/resume and dispose paths all behave. I made two fixes inside the module. (1) Overall output was too quiet: MASTER_GAIN was 0.5, which put music at -31 dBFS RMS and effects at -26 dBFS. I raised it to 0.85, so music is now -26.3 and effects -21.1, and effects stay 5.2 dB louder than music. Clipping is still impossible because the limiter curve never outputs more than 1, which caps the speakers at about 0.85; the measured worst pile-up is 0.80. (2) On mobile, if the browser stopped the AudioContext by itself (a phone call, an iOS interruption, or a resume() refused outside a gesture after the tab returns), sound stayed dead for the rest of the visit, because nothing calls unlock() after PRESS START. The engine now watches ctx.onstatechange, and when the context is stopped without the app having asked for it, the next tap, click or key press revives it. This never overrides an app suspend() for a hidden tab, and the listeners are removed on dispose. I added two lifecycle checks for this (32 of 32 pass) and tied the harness waveform scale to MASTER_GAIN. Type-check is clean.
requirementChecks: PASS - All 17 SfxName effects: window.__audioTest() renders each through an OfflineAudioContext. None is silent or clipping. Output peaks run from 0.22 (step) to 0.57 (starPose) after the gain change, and pitch contours go the intended way (uiSelect up, uiBack down, warpIn up and warpOut its mirror).

PASS - Three seamless loops: __audioMixTest shows each voice written to exactly the loop's step count (128 / 96 / 96). The third pass minus the second is -145 to -146 dB, while the same comparison one bar short is +2.4 to +2.6 dB, so the loop period is really the full loop. Level at the seam is within 1.1 dB of the loop average and there is no click.
PASS - Live scheduler: __audioLiveTest('title') error -131 dB and __audioLiveTest('lobby') -132.7 dB across the loop seam. No dropped or doubled notes.

PASS - Original compositions and sounds: the melodies are hand-written in G major, F major 3/4 and a music-box arpeggio, and the effects are generic synth recipes. I found no Nintendo or other game melody, signature sound, name or voice. Originality is judged by review only; nobody can prove a melody resembles nothing.
PASS - Silent until unlock(): play, setMusic, setMuted, suspend and resume before unlock create no AudioContext (lifecycle checks). The remembered track and mute state are applied on unlock.
FIXED - Level: music was quieter than effects, as required, but both were very quiet (music -30.9 dBFS RMS). With MASTER_GAIN at 0.85, music is -26.3 and effects -21.1, still 5.2 dB apart.
PASS - No clipping: limiter output is at most 1, times 0.85 master. Worst measured pile-up is 0.80 (threshold 0.98), and live analyser output stays below the clipping line.
PASS - Mute: a mute set before unlock is honoured (analyser reads silence), and toggling mid-cross-fade ramps without a click.

FIXED - Suspend/resume robustness: suspend freezes the clock and resume continues from the same loop position. A context the browser stopped on its own now comes back on the next gesture (new check: 'a system-suspended context is revived by the next gesture'). An app suspend() is not undone by a gesture (new check).

PASS - Dispose: closes the context, re-locks the engine, and leaves every later call safe. Unlock after dispose starts fresh and keeps the mute preference. Gesture listeners and onstatechange are now cleared too.
PASS - Safe without Web Audio or with a throwing constructor: every call is a silent no-op.

PASS - Integration cadence: the engine plays a step every ~0.29 s and a snore every 3.6 s, both above the module's rate limits (0.12 s and 2.8 s), so no sounds are dropped. It calls suspend/resume on visibilitychange.
PASS - Performance: calls rejected by the rate limiter return before allocating anything. The scheduler allocates only Web Audio nodes for notes, and finished voice chains are disconnected.

PASS - Harness page /dev/audio: renders correctly on desktop (1280x720 and 1280x1400) and mobile (390x844). All buttons are real <button>s and the sliders are labelled. reduced-motion does not apply to audio.
issuesFixed: Output was too quiet: MASTER_GAIN 0.5 gave music about -31 dBFS RMS and peaks of only 0.09 to 0.33. Raised to 0.85 in src/game/audio/synth.ts, with a comment explaining why clipping still cannot happen (output cannot exceed about 0.85).

Mobile audio stayed dead after a system interruption or a refused background resume, because nothing calls unlock() after PRESS START. src/game/audio/index.ts now arms capture-phase, passive pointerdown/pointerup/touchend/keydown/click listeners while the context is stopped without the app asking for it (ctx.onstatechange plus a check after unlock and resume). The next gesture calls unlock(). The listeners are removed when the context is running again, on an app suspend(), and on dispose.
Harness waveforms were drawn against a hard-coded 0.5 scale. src/app/dev/audio/page.tsx now uses MASTER_GAIN, so the louder output is not drawn out of range.
Added two lifecycle checks in src/app/dev/audio/tests.ts covering the self-heal and the rule that a gesture never undoes an app suspend().
issuesRemaining: Nobody has listened to the sounds; everything is checked numerically and visually. A person should audition /dev/audio, especially the doorOpen creak and the starPose fanfare, and how the loops feel on repeat.
Safari, iOS and Firefox are not tested; only headless Chrome was run. The iOS ringer switch still mutes Web Audio by default; this is intentional, since navigator.audioSession was not changed.
Low-end effects (doorClose, land, percussion kick) will sound thin on phone speakers.
src/game/services.ts still points at the stub audio. Switching it to `./audio` is the integration step and is not this module's file.
integrationNotes: Switch src/game/services.ts to `import { createAudio } from "./audio"`. The contract interface is unchanged.
Mixer levels are now MASTER_GAIN 0.85, SFX_GAIN 1.2, MUSIC_GAIN 0.26. If music should come up after a listening pass, raise MUSIC_GAIN; clipping cannot happen at any setting.
UI code does not need to call unlock() on later gestures any more: the engine revives a context the browser stopped by itself on the next tap or key press. Calling unlock() anyway is still harmless.
The engine already calls suspend()/resume() on visibilitychange, as the module expects.
verification: npx tsc --noEmit -p . : exit 0, no errors (before and after the fixes).
node shot.mjs http://localhost:3000/dev/audio with eval window.__audioTest(): 20 rows, all OK. Effect peaks after the fix are 0.22 to 0.57 and music peaks 0.15 to 0.23.
window.__audioMixTest(): every loop passes, options pass, cross-fade passes. Pile-up output peak 0.80 (pre-limiter 1.20), clipping false. Music -26.3 dB and effects -21.1 dB, effects 5.2 dB louder.
window.__audioLifecycleTest(): 30/30 before the fixes and 32/32 after (two new self-heal checks).
window.__audioLiveTest('title') and ('lobby'): pass, errors -131.2 dB and -132.7 dB.

Screenshots (opened and inspected) in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-faviojasso-Library-Application-Support-Claude-scratch-workspaces-2e78f3bf-6b09-4892-8e37-05d4f25b71e0-0f59886b-c83f-4098-9822-b751fbbcfb93-scratch-2026-11-10-cf9e80/381bbed9-222e-45b2-b07f-9df9e8e2450e/scratchpad/shots/review-audio/ : after-tests.png, initial.png, mobile.png (390x844), results.png (full results table with waveforms at ±0.85 and spectrograms).
The only driver noise is the unrelated va.vercel-scripts.com analytics request blocked by ORB. There were no page errors.
